`silero_vad.int8.onnx` is Silero VAD (MIT, © Silero Team, https://github.com/snakers4/silero-vad), quantised to int8 by the sherpa-onnx project and published with its release `asr-models` (https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx/releases/download/asr-models/silero_vad.int8.onnx, SHA-256 `c36d490aff5ab924ca6c7aeec4d8f6bd3d22db6fa17611b9c5b17eae58ac3a20`). The ONNX Runtime test runs it in both runtimes the app ships.

`openai-mixed.json` and `soniox-mixed.json` are what OpenAI's live transcription (`gpt-live-transcribe`) and Soniox's real-time model (`stt-rt-v5`) sent back on 2026-10-19 for FLEURS clips (CC BY 4.0) in English and Mandarin taking turns, recorded with `INCARNAMIND_EVAL_RECORD` (eval/transcription/routes.transcription.ts). OpenAI's keeps the first ten turns and only the events the adapter reads; Soniox's keeps the first 40 seconds, every message with final text and one in six of the rest, without confidences. The adapters' contract tests play them back.

`qwen-en.json`, `qwen-zh.json` and `qwen-mixed.json` are not recordings. They are written to the format Alibaba Cloud documents for Fun-ASR real-time recognition's server events (`task-started`, `result-generated` with its sentence and heartbeat packets, `task-finished`), with sentences in the style of FLEURS (CC BY 4.0) read speech in English and Mandarin. They stand in until `INCARNAMIND_EVAL_RECORD` can record what the service sends, which needs a Qwen key. The adapter's contract tests play them back.
